claim: For the real regular octagonal plane \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where \(N(x,y)=\max\{|x|,|y|,(|x|+|y|)/\sqrt2\}\), the Ptolemy constant is exactly \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)=4-2\sqrt2\).

correctness.rationale: The sharp global comparison \(\cos(\pi/8)\|v\|_2\le N(v)\le\|v\|_2\) is proved by a complete one-variable minimization after exhausting norm symmetries. Euclidean Ptolemy gives the exact candidate upper bound \(4-2\sqrt2\), and an explicit admissible triple attains that number. All displayed norm values and radical identities were symbolically rechecked.

evidence: Zuo (2018), Example 1, treats \(\max\{\|\cdot\|_p,\lambda\|\cdot\|_q\}\) but states the mixed-regime formula for \(\lambda>2^{1/2-1/q}\); for \(q=1\) the regular octagon is the omitted endpoint.
For Theorem 7 with Euclidean comparison, \(M_1=\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}>1\), so the required \(\sqrt2 M_1\) lies above the regular octagon\'s James-function maximum \(\sqrt2\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The later broader framework was inspected rather than assumed noncovering from titles. Its displayed example and its general symmetric theorem do not directly imply the endpoint equality.

evidence: The norm is exactly \(\max\{\|\cdot\|_\infty,2^{-1/2}\|\cdot\|_1\}\), so it is the \((p,q,\lambda)=(\infty,1,1/\sqrt2)\) endpoint of Zuo\'s max-norm family.
Its absolute-normalized function is \(\psi(t)=\max\{1-t,t,1/\sqrt2\}\). The ratio \(\psi_2/\psi\) is maximized at the branch transition, not at \(1/2\).

value.rationale: The regular octagonal plane is a classical benchmark explicitly used in the James-constant literature, and the Ptolemy constant is a standard metric-geometric invariant. The claim gives an exact natural invariant, exhibits a sharp extremal triple, and resolves the natural endpoint of a published max-norm family rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The coincidence of the upper comparison bound with an attainable ratio is structurally informative for polygonal Banach planes.
